scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Model D3
models.what_it_computes: A detailed 3D implicit finite element model of the optic–haptic assembly in contact with a deforming capsular bag that computes haptic stresses, capsule–haptic contact pressures, and optic tilt/decentration under prescribed capsular contraction.

models.name: Model RB
models.what_it_computes: A reduced-order implicit finite element ring–beam model that represents the capsule as a contracting ring and the haptics as curved beams connected to a rigid optic, computing global stiffness, peak beam stress, and optic kinematics under contraction loads.

mechanisms.name: Uniform equatorial contracture
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Circumferential shrinkage of the equator elevates haptic loads, risking optic tilt and haptic overstress during postoperative capsular bag fibrosis.

mechanisms.name: Sectoral fibrosis with directional shrinkage
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Localized contraction in a capsular sector drives asymmetric contact and tilt/decentration, a clinically observed failure mode leading to visual disturbances.

mechanisms.name: Anterior capsulorhexis phimosis
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Contraction of the anterior capsule rim increases anterior edge tension and can impinge on haptic crowns, altering load paths and inducing malposition.

deviation.detail: All credibility factors and overall model risk are rated on a 0–4 Credibility Index (0=None, 1=Low, 2=Moderate, 3=High, 4=Very High).

expected_decision.outcome_source: Under the adopted Credibility Index of 3/4, we judge the evidence sufficient to use the two models to down-select haptic design variants and to omit additional benchtop capsular bag simulant testing for the screened mechanisms when margins are ample as defined by the design gates.

expected_context_of_use: The purpose of these predictions is to provide the primary evidence to select among haptic design variants and to justify omission of additional benchtop capsular bag simulant tests for those scenarios where the simulations show unambiguous margin.

spans: The detailed model identifies contact patch extents of about 110° on either side of the haptic crowns, with smooth pressure gradients and no localized spikes, further supporting this conclusion.

Under uniform equatorial contracture (8% circumferential shrinkage), Model D3 predicts peak haptic stress of 41 MPa, equatorial contact pressure of 38 kPa, optic tilt of 0.47°, and decentration of 0.08 mm; Model RB predicts 39 MPa, 36 kPa, 0.42°, and 0.09 mm, respectively.
The interaction between the device and bag is mediated by surface contact with friction.
findings.span: The detailed model identifies contact patch extents of about 110° on either side of the haptic crowns, with smooth pressure gradients and no localized spikes, further supporting this conclusion.

spans: For uniform equatorial contracture, 8% circumferential shrinkage is applied with sensitivity runs at 6% and 10%.

Variation across the ranges reported above changes the computed peak haptic stress by less than 10% under uniform contraction and by 10–18% under sectoral and phimosis scenarios, while optic tilt and decentration shift by less than 0.1° and 0.05 mm under uniform contraction and up to 0.3° and 0.06 mm in asymmetric cases.
findings.span: For uniform equatorial contracture, 8% circumferential shrinkage is applied with sensitivity runs at 6% and 10%.

spans: Over indentation depths up to 0.2 mm and shell thicknesses 10–20 µm, force errors were below 1.1% and peak pressure errors below 1.8%.

Third, a volumetric patch test: a small Model D3 submodel with mixed solid and shell elements under uniform strain states showed stress equilibrium to machine precision with residual force norms below 1e9 N and displacement errors below 1e7 mm, indicating correct element formulations and coupling.
findings.span: Over indentation depths up to 0.2 mm and shell thicknesses 10–20 µm, force errors were below 1.1% and peak pressure errors below 1.8%.

spans: For Model D3 under uniform equatorial contracture at 8% shrinkage, increasing the device mesh from approximately 80,000 to 320,000 elements and refining the equatorial shell elements from 0.4 mm to 0.2 mm reduced changes in peak haptic von Mises stress to 2.8%, optic tilt to 0.05°, and equatorial contact pressure to 1.6 kPa.
Contact stabilization energy remained below 0.4% of total strain energy throughout the solution, indicating limited regularization influence.

spans: Sectoral fibrosis is represented by 12% shrinkage over a 90° sector, with sensitivity runs at 10% and 14% and sector extent 60–120°.
Increasing sector extent to 120° or shrinkage to 14% drives Model D3 stress to 66–68 MPa and tilt to 1.6–1.9°, squeezing the margins.

spans: For Model D3 under sectoral fibrosis at 12% shrinkage over a 90° sector, the same mesh refinement reduced peak stress changes from 9.1% to 5.9% and tilt changes from 0.31° to 0.18°, with decentration stabilizing within 0.03 mm.
Contact stabilization energy peaked at 1.2% during transitions of the active contact patch near sector edges.

spans: Anterior capsulorhexis phimosis is represented by 25% rim shrinkage, with sensitivity at 20% and 30%.
